result.topic_en: Ramanujan gives examples of integrals of arctan(x^3)/(e^{2πnx}-1) evaluated in finite terms, then decomposes an alternating series sum (-1)^{n-1} n^2/(n^3+α^3) and an integral of x^5/(sinh πx (α^6+x^6)) into partial-fraction series that can be summed in finite terms when α is an odd integer.
result.transcription:
Add. Ms a 94 18 (58) (58) (3)
can be expressed in finite terms for all positive integral values of $\alpha$. Thus for example
$\int_0^\infty \frac{\tan^{-1}x^3}{e^{2\pi x}-1}dx = \frac{1}{4}\log 2\pi - \frac{1}{2}\log(1+e^{-\pi\sqrt{3}}) - \frac{\pi}{4\sqrt{3}}$;
$\int_0^\infty \frac{\tan^{-1}x^3}{e^{4\pi x}-1}dx = \frac{1}{8}\log 12\pi - \frac{1}{4}\log(1-e^{-2\pi\sqrt{3}}) - \frac{\pi}{4\sqrt{3}}$;
and so on.
4. It is easy to see that
(11) $\frac{1^2}{1^3+\alpha^3} - \frac{2^2}{2^3+\alpha^3} + \frac{3^2}{3^3+\alpha^3} - \frac{4^2}{4^3+\alpha^3} + \cdots$
$= \frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{1+\alpha} - \frac{1}{2+\alpha} + \frac{1}{3+\alpha} - \frac{1}{4+\alpha} + \cdots\right)$
$+ \frac{4}{3}\left\{\frac{2-\alpha}{(2-\alpha)^2+3\alpha^2} - \frac{4-\alpha}{(4-\alpha)^2+3\alpha^2} + \frac{6-\alpha}{(6-\alpha)^2+3\alpha^2} - \cdots\right\}$.
Since
$\frac{1}{1^2+x^2} - \frac{3}{3^2+x^2} + \frac{5}{5^2+x^2} - \cdots = \frac{\pi}{4}\operatorname{sech}\frac{\pi x}{2}$,
we see that the left hand side of (11) can be expressed in finite terms if $\alpha$ is any odd integer. For example
$\frac{1^2}{1^3+1} - \frac{2^2}{2^3+1} + \frac{3^2}{3^3+1} - \cdots = \frac{1}{3}(1-\log 2 + \pi\operatorname{sech}\frac{1}{2}\pi\sqrt{3})$.
Again, if $\alpha > 0$, then
(12) $\int_0^\infty \frac{x^5}{\sinh\pi x}\cdot\frac{dx}{\alpha^6+x^6} = \frac{2}{\pi}\int_0^\infty\left\{\frac{1}{2x^2} + \sum_{n=1}^{n=\infty}\frac{(-1)^n}{n^2+x^2}\right\}\frac{x^6\,dx}{\alpha^6+x^6}$
$= \frac{1}{3}\left(\frac{1}{\alpha} - \frac{1}{1+\alpha} + \frac{1}{2+\alpha} - \frac{1}{3+\alpha} + \cdots\right)$
$- \frac{4}{3}\left\{\frac{2+\alpha}{(2+\alpha)^2+3\alpha^2} - \frac{4+\alpha}{(4+\alpha)^2+3\alpha^2} + \frac{6+\alpha}{(6+\alpha)^2+3\alpha^2} - \cdots\right\}$.
Hence the left-hand side of (12) can be expressed in finite terms if $\alpha$ is any odd integer. For example
$\int_0^\infty \frac{x^5}{\sinh\pi x}\cdot\frac{dx}{1+x^6} = \frac{1}{3}(\log 2 - 1 + \pi\operatorname{sech}\frac{1}{2}\pi\sqrt{3})$.
